questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Sugar tastes sweet.

options.text: Sugar is sweet when it has been tasted sweet.
Sugar is sweet when it is tasted.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sugar is sweet when it is tasted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in present indefinite tense and in active voice.
 
• The rules for changing simple present indefinite tense in passive voice are: 
 
 
• The following structure should be followed when verbs are followed by adjectives:
 
• Active voice :Sub + Verb + Adj 

 Passive voice: Sub + Verb + Adj + when + pronoun + H.V + V3 
 
 
• ​Example: Rose smells sweet. (Active)

 Rose is sweet when it is smelt. (Passive)
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence the expression 'sugar tastes sweet' should be written as 'sugar is sweet when it is tasted' in 'passive voice'.
 
• Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

 

Correct sentence: Sugar is sweet when it is tasted.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.

options.text: A taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a tortilla topped with a filling.
A taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of an tortilla topped with filling.
An taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of tortilla topped with filling.
A taco is traditional Mexican dish consisting of a tortilla topped with an filling.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is A taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a tortilla topped with a filling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indefinite article:An article that refers to a noun without specifying it or refers to a noun to introduce it for the first time.
 
• There are two indefinite articles: A and An. 
 
• A: Used before a word that begins with a consonant.
 
 
• Example: She found a penny on the ground. (P is a consonant.) 
 
 
 
• An: Used before a word that begins with a vowel. 
 
 
• Example: He ate an apple. (A is a vowel.)
 
 
 
• Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

 

Correct sentence: ***A**__ taco is __**a**__ traditional Mexican dish consisting of __**a**__ tortilla topped with __**a**__ filling.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

You must not __insists on help__ people who don't want it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"insist on helping"** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses **"insists on help people," **which is grammatically incorrect because **"insists" **should not be in the third person singular form when used with **"You must not."**
 
• The correct phrase is **"insist on helping," **which means to persist in helping someone despite their resistance.
 
• **"Insist on" **is the correct prepositional phrase to use when expressing the action of persistently trying to do something.
 
• **"Helping" **is the gerund form of **"help," **which is necessary after the preposition **"on" **to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the phrase **"insist on helping" **correctly matches the subject **"You" **and properly conveys the intended meaning of persistently trying to offer assistance.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, **"insist for helping," **is incorrect because **"for" **is not the appropriate preposition to use with **"insist" **in this context.
 
• Option 3, **"insists of help," **is incorrect because **"insists of" **is not a grammatically correct or meaningful phrase in English, and **"insists" **should not be used with **"You."**
 
• Option 4, **"insist to help," **is incorrect because **"to help" **does not convey the meaning of persistent action that **"on helping" **does which is needed in this context.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

• The segment **"soundly slept" **is incorrect because it disrupts the natural word order in English for adverbs and verbs in this context.
 
• In the correct English syntax, the adverb **'soundly' **should come after the auxiliary verb **'had' **and before the main verb **'slept.'**
 
• Therefore, the corrected segment should read **"had not slept soundly."**

• It correctly describes the child's state of being using the verb 'was.'
 
 
 
• **"the previous night" **is also correct.
 
 
• It properly specifies the time frame being discussed with no grammatical issues.
 
 
 
• **"because she had not" **does not contain a grammatical error on its own.
 
 
• It sets up a cause-effect relationship that is grammatically sound.
